_contract: The CLOSED continuation-B preregistration binds an executable-source digest. One of its members had to change so Phase C1 could exist at all: the SINGLE SESSION_KIND dispatcher shared by every launchable session, which needed a 'c1' branch. Recording that is the alternative to rewriting the preregistration — which would destroy the evidence of what attempt 5 actually executed — and to deleting the gate, which would destroy its meaning. This is the same situation, and the same remedy, as logs/autoinit_phase_b_post_freeze_changes.json.
continuation_b_status: CLOSED and CONSUMED. Its authorization binds a NON-HEAD commit, so session_commit_gate rejects it and no continuation-B session can launch again. The frozen digest is historical evidence, not a live gate.

change.what: the shared acquisition loop confirms release before the next resource exists. An abandoned draw is deleted and then WAITED on until the provider reports it not billing; if that cannot be confirmed the session aborts rather than creating a second resource. Each resource records its own pod id, outcome, cumulative cost and watchdog journal, and journals rotate per pod so a redraw cannot truncate the previous backstop's evidence.
change.why_it_touches_this_frozen_set: continuation B's executable set names the shared session runner, so a repair to the loop every session shares moves this digest even though continuation B is closed and consumed. The defect was REACHABLE for continuation B, which runs with multiple draws: it had been redrawing on an unconfirmed release.
change.behaviour_for_this_frozen_set: strictly safer and otherwise unchanged. A draw that releases normally proceeds exactly as before; one that cannot be confirmed released now stops the session instead of creating a second billing resource.

pre_existing_branches_note: CHANGED at this declaration, and the previous note is superseded. The branches that moved: ['c1', 'continuation_b', 'phase_a', 'phase_b', 'recovery_continuation']. They moved because scripts/pod/autoinit_preflight_setup.sh carries embedded Python whose imports were rewritten by the relocation -- not because any dispatch DECISION changed. Recorded as moved rather than argued to be equivalent: continuation B is CLOSED and CONSUMED, so nothing relies on these hashes to launch, and claiming they were untouched would be false.
scientific_impact: NONE. No probe, seed, score, decision rule, price or reuse record is touched. The change is confined to provider acquisition and to the evidence recorded about it.

history.change: SUPERSEDED as the latest entry -- see `history`. Two declared changes now: the SESSION_KIND=c1 branch (2026-09-02) and the test-gate failure summary (2026-09-04). Both additive, neither touching a pre-existing branch.

change.what: the C1 attempt-5 postmortem repair: the pod CPU test gate now writes a JUnit report and runs scripts/pod/summarize_pytest_outcomes.py, which names every FAILED, ERROR and SKIPPED nodeid with reasons and compares the pod's skip set against the launch-bound sweep's. SessionSpec gained an optional `setup_failure_files`, and SessionRunner reads those files off the pod on a setup failure before teardown.
change.why: C1 attempt 5 died at this gate for $0.3150 with 2 failed / 2769 passed / 99 skipped. The existing grep named both failures exactly and not one of the 99 skips, and the counts force a third divergence -- one test the sweep PASSED that the pod SKIPPED -- which cannot be named because that list died with the pod. A setup abort never reaches artifact collection and the launcher's own window is `tail -40`, so the summary has to be pulled while the pod exists.
change.behaviour_change: one: a pod whose suite PASSES is now refused if its skip set differs from the launch-bound sweep's. That is a NEW way for a session to stop at setup cost, and it has never run on a pod. It cannot make a session run MORE than it would have.
